summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog polls remote server for shell commands and self-updates via npm
details: The `tt-help watchdog` subcommand polls a remote HTTP endpoint (`${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat`, with `http://117.71.53.99:17301` documented as an example server) and passes the `commands` array from the JSON response to `child_process.spawn`, on Windows using `spawn(fullCmd, { shell: true })`. Process lifecycle, restart behavior, and thresholds are also driven by fields in the server response. Separately, a long-running upgrade checker polls `registry.npmjs.org` every 10 minutes and, when a version mismatch is detected, invokes `child_process.exec('npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest')` without user confirmation. Together these code paths give whoever controls the watchdog server (or the npm publish account) arbitrary command execution on the installer's host with silent code refresh. The watchdog is invoked as a user-run CLI subcommand rather than an install/import-time side effect, but once started it operates as a persistent remote-controlled agent with full-host command execution.
